text:
maria: FYI customer NorthPoint reporting sudden p99 spikes on embeddings API since ~09:30 UTC, affecting batch workloads. They say one of their jobs that usually completes in <2s per request is now 6-12s. Example request id: req_0a1b2c3d.
ethan: thanks, any tenant id / region? is this hosted or dedicated?
maria: hosted-us-west, tenant id np-981. They only use embeddings endpoint, batch size 16, model: openembed-3b-quant. Happening across multiple nodes per their logs.
leah: pinging @northpoint CS contact — asked for a repro payload and whether they saw increased qps.
maria: repro curl they sent: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" -d '{"model":"openembed-3b-quant","input":[...16 items...]}'` — latency sampled 9s for a single item in batch. They saw it only on certain time windows.
ethan: can you drop the full request_ids (ideally 3) + the server-side request ids? I want to correlate with agent logs. I'll check host-level metrics (cpu/gpu mem, queue length).
sanjay: looks like a classic noisy-tenant pattern. We saw small bursts of long KV-cache misses on that model after recent kernel update. Also check per-tenant concurrency and queueing.
ops-bot: alert: embeddings.p99 > 5s for tenant np-981 between 09:28-09:41 UTC (p95=2.3s p99=7.8s). Affected nodes: gpu-node-13,gpu-node-14. Triggered runbook: embeddings-tail.
ethan: thanks. I'll pull the per-tenant queue depth and scheduler logs. If KV cache miss rate high, fallback to cold path increases latency.
maria: sent request_ids: srv_req_20240322_az1_req12345, srv_req_20240322_az1_req12387, srv_req_20240322_az1_req12412. Also attached their raw payload in ticket.
ethan: correlating... I see those on gpu-node-13 with spike in host CPU and preemption events at 09:30. There are other tenants with bursty embedding jobs at same time — likely noisy neighbor.
sanjay: quick mitigation options: 1) apply temporary per-tenant reservation (reserve extra slots) for np-981, 2) add them to short-lived allowlist for burst concurrency, 3) enact adaptive throttling on offending tenant(s). Which does CS want?
maria: customer wants a short-term fix while we root cause. Prefer reservation if it's fast. They asked for an ETA.
ethan: we can create a temporary reservation for 2 extra slots in that AZ within 10-15m. I'll also add a routing rule to prefer nodes with lower cache churn. Command (admin API):
```
curl -X POST https://control.redwood.internal/v1/admin/reservations \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \ 
  -d '{"tenant_id":"np-981","region":"us-west-1","slots":2,"ttl_minutes":60}'
```
I'll run it and post the job id.
leah: also offering customer a small client-side workaround: reduce batch size to 8 to avoid long tail while we stabilize. Communicated this to NorthPoint.
ops-bot: action: reservation created job_id resv_7789 by ethan at 09:52 UTC.
maria: applied and customer confirms improved latency in their next run: p99 dropped to ~2.1s. They see much less tail. :partyparrot:
ethan: creating follow-up task to investigate kernel change impact on KV cache evictions. Filing an infra bug: INFRA-4892. We'll examine model kernel rollout, eviction thresholds, and scheduler fairness.
sanjay: also will add a short-term throttle on the noisy tenant(s) identified (tenant id tn-442) to prevent recurrence.
maria: customer happy for now, asked for timeline on permanent fix. I'll schedule a sync with them next week and keep ticket open.
ethan: marking thread for postmortem and tagging eng-runtime + sched team. Short notes: noisy-tenant -> cache churn -> cold-path p99 spike; mitigation: reservation + batch-size suggestion + throttle.
leah: noted. Closing loop with customer and adding runbook step to consider reservation before throttling in similar cases.
maria: thanks all :heart:
